oneFilter.intro: Before I say yes to anything, or pick what to work on, run it through this:
questions: Does it move D-One toward autonomous? (Client's + contractor's favourite subcontractor · interchangeable humans · Darren out one month at a time.) Or is it just chase-mode?
Is it the current bottleneck? (Growth Wheel.) Or a shiny distraction from the real constraint?
Do I have capacity? I am a basket — rest fills it, output empties it. Am I resting as much as I'm outputting? Am I inside my 20% buffer?
If it's a deal: Is it what we actually want, and do we hold the power seat? The one willing to walk away has the most power.

Is this slot actually free? A blank space is not automatically free — before I say yes, check the board for what else could have gone there (surf, rest, family, focus). Every yes is a no to something else.

parkingLot.title: 🤝 Social Investment System — the 15
parkingLot.text: Proactive social plan. One intentional touchpoint/week: pull the top name off the queue, make the plan, send it to the back.
notes: TRACK 1 — NEIGHBOURS (Val de Vie + Boschendal, 10). Logistically trivial. Rhythm = one recurring anchor (padel/surf/coffee/braai), rotate 2-3 through each time. People: Justin Drennan, Mike Dixon, James Iron, Simon Raab, Andrew Gait Golding, Jonathan Cornish, Paul Rowett, Alistair Simpson, Hardi Swart (all Val de Vie) + Tal Aviram (Boschendal, ~15 min).

TRACK 2 — INTENTIONAL (5). Slip if not scheduled. Cape Town (Brett Jordaan, Jon Ratcliffe, Brad Morgan) = monthly catch-up rotating through the three. Dom Peters (touring) = catch when he's through CT. Vince Dickson (USA) = quarterly call + in-person when travelling.

ROTATING QUEUE (one/week, then send to back; interleaves far people so they don't slip): 1 Justin Drennan | 2 Mike Dixon | 3 Tal Aviram | 4 Brett Jordaan (CT) | 5 James Iron | 6 Simon Raab | 7 Jon Ratcliffe (CT) | 8 Andrew Gait Golding | 9 Vince Dickson (USA call) | 10 Jonathan Cornish | 11 Brad Morgan (CT) | 12 Paul Rowett | 13 Alistair Simpson | 14 Dom Peters (or call if not local) | 15 Hardi Swart → repeat.

WEEKLY RITUAL: at your weekly review, take the top queue name, propose a REAL date, move them to the back. Neighbours you'll also see incidentally on top of this — the queue is the floor, not the ceiling.
RULE: never send 'we should catch up' — always propose a specific day/activity. That's the whole difference between intention and drift.
